mission.heading: Our Mission
mission.text: Italian Football Pathways is an educational company that specializes in helping Ukrainian students access quality education in sports management in Italy. We believe every talented student deserves the opportunity to study at Europe's best universities.

Over 5 years, we've helped more than 200 students launch their careers in sports management.

hero.title: Frequently Asked Questions
hero.subtitle: Answers to the most common questions about studying in Italy

items.question: What are the requirements for admission to a sports management program?
items.answer: For a bachelor's degree, you need a secondary school diploma. For a master's, a bachelor's degree is required. For an MBA, you need a master's degree and at least 3 years of professional experience. A language certificate is also required (IELTS/TOEFL for English-taught programs or CILS/CELI for Italian-taught programs).

items.question: How much does tuition cost?
items.answer: Costs vary by program and university. Bachelor's: from €1,000 to €4,000 per year at public universities. Master's: from €2,000 to €8,000 per year. MBA programs: from €30,000 to €50,000 for the full course. We help with finding scholarships and grants.

items.question: Are there programs taught in English?
items.answer: Yes, many master's and MBA programs are fully available in English. Bachelor's programs are mostly in Italian, but there are exceptions. We recommend learning Italian alongside your studies for better integration.

items.question: How do I get a student visa for Italy?
items.answer: To obtain a type D student visa, you need: an acceptance letter from the university, proof of financial means (approximately €6,000 per year), health insurance, and housing. We fully guide you through this process.

items.question: How long does the visa process take?
items.answer: Typically, the process takes 4–8 weeks after submitting documents to the consulate. We recommend starting document preparation 3–4 months before the start of your studies.

items.question: How much does it cost to live in Italy?
items.answer: Average student expenses: €700–€1,200 per month depending on the city. Rome and Milan are more expensive (€900–€1,200), while smaller cities are cheaper (€600–€800). This includes housing, food, transport, and personal expenses.

items.question: Can I work while studying?
items.answer: Yes, a student visa allows you to work up to 20 hours per week. Many of our students find part-time jobs at sports organizations, gaining both income and professional experience.

items.question: Is there a Ukrainian community in Italy?
items.answer: Italy is home to one of the largest Ukrainian communities in Europe — approximately 240,000 people. Major cities have Ukrainian churches, shops, and cultural centers. Our students also form their own support community.

items.question: What career opportunities are available after graduation?
items.answer: Graduates work at football clubs, sports federations, marketing agencies, media companies, and event organizers. Positions include: sports manager, marketer, scout, analyst, and event coordinator.

items.question: Do you help with job placement?
items.answer: Yes, we provide career support: CV preparation to European standards, interview coaching, and access to our network of contacts in the sports industry. 95% of our graduates are employed within 6 months of completing their studies.
